title: 10. Linear Regression & Evaluation
description: Build simple and multiple linear regression models and measure R², MSE, and MAE.

blocks.content:
### Linear Regression Fundamentals

Simple Linear Regression fits a best-fit line:

$$y = m \cdot x + b$$

![Linear Regression Line Fit](/images/ml/chart_linear_regression.png)

#### Polynomial Regression for Nonlinear Relationships
When relationships curve, add polynomial features ($x^2, x^3$) to capture non-linear fits.

![Polynomial Fit vs Linear Fit](/images/ml/chart_polynomial_fit.png)

Linear regression draws the straight trend that best summarizes a relationship, such as how study hours tend to relate to a score. It then uses that trend to estimate a new value.

It predicts a number, not a guaranteed future. A good-looking line can still be wrong when the pattern curves, has unusual points, or changes over time.

blocks.starterCode:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score, mean_squared_error

X = np.array([[1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6]])
y = np.array([52, 58, 65, 72, 80, 88])

model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

preds = model.predict(X)
print(f'Slope (m): {model.coef_[0]:.2f}')
print(f'R^2 Score: {r2_score(y, preds):.4f}')
blocks.solutionCode:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score, mean_squared_error

X = np.array([[1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6]])
y = np.array([52, 58, 65, 72, 80, 88])
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)
preds = model.predict(X)
print(f'Slope (m): {model.coef_[0]:.2f}')
print(f'R^2 Score: {r2_score(y, preds):.4f}')
